experiment.description: Only the exact selection isU32 body is replaced. No hot predicate observers, queue logging, browser recorders or Rust changes. HTTP identity metadata is fetched after each workload.
experiment.servedResponseCheck: A direct GET of the selection module on the active test server contains the bit guard and no numeric-predicate or selection-point observer wrappers. Playwright's saved network record had no JavaScript response body; this is a separate server-response check, not a trace-body attestation.

predicateCost.method: Blank browser realm, both exact function bodies compiled before measurement. Float64Array inputs, 1000000 calls per timed arm, two warmups per arm, nine alternating-order pairs per workload, three independent cases per engine. No concurrent Breditor stress/build jobs; unrelated host activity is not controlled.
predicateCost.correctness: Every arm must match an independent accepted-input count; invalid samples fail the test rather than contribute timings.
predicateCost.rawSamples: selection-u32-cost.json attachment in each of the nine retained traces
predicateCost.summaryUnits: Approximate nanoseconds per input; medians of the three per-case medians. Rounded values reflect clock quantization, not nanosecond clock precision.

candidate.coverage: Six clipboard boundary cases, rejected paste, and 10000-restores stress in each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

original.scope: Smoke check for the unmodified control and metadata path, not matched original-arm stress or evidence that the original bug is resolved.

limits: This is a candidate compatibility change, not a repair to WebKit itself. Earlier numeric and JavaScript-only failures remain valid evidence.
The clipboard workload uses real DOM selections and controlled clipboard events, not the system clipboard.
These runs do not qualify native Safari, iOS, or every numeric predicate in the application.
The timing comparison is an isolated indirect-call microbenchmark, not production editor latency or a performance pass/fail threshold.
A candidate passing stress does not invalidate the historical original-guard failures or establish that every WebKit failure has the same cause.
Generated output and traces are local ignored artifacts. Preserve their recorded bytes before rebuilding into the same directories.
